title: K-Pop Just Went Punjabi. LE SSERAFIM and Guru Randhawa Made a Track That Shouldn't Work — and It Absolutely Slaps.
excerpt: The biggest K-pop girl group on earth tapped India's most streamed Punjabi artist for a BOOMPALA remix that mixes Korean, English, Spanish, and Punjabi into one festival anthem. This is what the future sounds like.
body:
Here is a sentence nobody expected to read in 2026: five Korean pop stars and a Punjabi singer from Gurdaspur just made the most eclectic party anthem of the summer.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=0CEg8nz_I9U</youtube>

**LE SSERAFIM** — the HYBE-label quintet who have quietly become one of the biggest girl groups on the planet — released a collaborative remix of their hit single **BOOMPALA** featuring **Guru Randhawa** on June 6. It is the first time LE SSERAFIM has ever collaborated with an Indian artist. It is also Guru Randhawa's first official K-pop credit. And the result is, frankly, ridiculous in the best possible way.

The original BOOMPALA, off LE SSERAFIM's sophomore album *PUREFLOW Pt. 1*, was already a genre-blender — a Latin house track sampling the **Macarena**, sung in Korean, English, and Spanish, that entered the Billboard Bubbling Under Hot 100 at No. 10. The album itself debuted at No. 10 on the Billboard 200, giving the group their fifth consecutive Top 10 entry.

Now add Punjabi to the mix.

## What the Remix Actually Sounds Like

Randhawa does not phone this in. His verses arrive with the signature high-energy Punjabi vocal runs that made **Suit Suit**, **High Rated Gabru**, and **Lahore** inescapable across South Asian playlists worldwide. Against LE SSERAFIM's razor-sharp choreography and the track's thumping Latin house production, the Punjabi lyrics hit with a force that turns what was already a party starter into a genuine cross-continental festival anthem.

Indian fans were quick to catch the details — a 'namaste' woven into the lyrics, yoga-inspired moves in the choreography. These are not token gestures. They are the signatures of a collaboration where both sides clearly studied each other's playbooks.

> "LE SSERAFIM is incredible, and 'BOOMPALA' already has an infectious energy that reminds me of the massive, celebratory vibe we love in India. Bringing my style to a Latin-house K-pop track that samples 'Macarena' felt like a beautiful collision." — Guru Randhawa

The group reciprocated: LE SSERAFIM said Randhawa brought "entirely new, vibrant life" to the song.

## Why This Matters More Than a Feature Credit

K-pop and Indian pop have been circling each other for years. BTS has an enormous Indian fanbase. BLACKPINK's concerts in India drew record demand. Indian artists have covered K-pop hits, and Korean variety shows have featured Bollywood dance segments. But an actual collaborative recording between a top-tier K-pop act and a major Indian artist? That has not happened at this level before.

The deal was facilitated by **Warner Music India**, signaling that the label infrastructure is now actively building bridges between Seoul and Mumbai. For the Indian music industry — which has historically looked West for international crossovers — this eastward pivot could reshape how desi artists approach global collaboration.

## The Diaspora Angle

For South Asian listeners in the US, UK, and Canada, the BOOMPALA remix lands in a sweet spot. K-pop concert culture and desi party culture share more DNA than either fanbase might admit — the coordinated fan projects, the devotion to choreography, the sheer volume at which both communities play music in their cars. A track that genuinely fuses both? It's not just a novelty. It is a playlist staple waiting to happen.

Guru Randhawa, for his part, has been expanding his international footprint methodically — collaborations with **Pitbull**, **Jay Sean**, **The Chainsmokers**, **Rick Ross**, and **French Montana** already dot his discography. But the K-pop move is arguably his smartest yet. LE SSERAFIM's fanbase, known as FEARNOTs, is one of the most engaged in global pop. Every stream, every share, every fan edit carries exponential reach.

The BOOMPALA remix featuring Guru Randhawa is available now on all major streaming platforms. The original track has already crossed 18 million Spotify streams and 10 million YouTube views in its first four days. Watch for this one to become the soundtrack of every desi wedding DJ set and K-pop fan meetup from Brampton to Fremont through the rest of the summer.

Seoul called. Punjab picked up.
